page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre with page number at top right. A large map (engraving) occupies the upper part, with its caption "CAPUT XIII." and title "Navarra." below. Below that, one text column with paragraphs, line numbers 30, 40, 50 at the left edge, and marginal notes in the right margin beside the text. Under the text: a centred block of inscription lines (SEMPRONIAE etc.) with a side note "Euci legit Clusius", then the final paragraph running to the foot, ending with a line of signature-like inscription "X" and "NIOIP".

main_text.l: CAPUT XIII.
Navarra.
NAVARRA nomen novum est, recensque natum. Sic enim dicitur, ut quorun-
dam est conjectura, quod Hispani Navas vocent Areas Camporum planas,
arboribusque purgatas; quibus tamen in circuitu Silvæ sunt & Dumeta; unde
Navarra regio, quæ complures habet Navas. Pecori est agriculturæque valde com-
moda: &, quamvis Pyrenæis opposita, atque adeo montibus undique conclusa, fi-
nitimas tamen versus Hispaniæ interiora Provincias Acris clementia superat. De
Navarrorum gente multa Ioannes Gerundensis Episcopus Hispaniæ Paralipomen.
lib. v. Rodericus Sanctius part.i. cap. xii, & alij.
Habitarunt hic olim, qui Vascones Plinio Tacitoque; Ptolemæo Οὐάσκονες: quos
postea in Galliam transmigrasse constat. Berones, Βήρωνες Straboni & Ptolemæo, quos
ille antea Tyrios notat vocatos: nomen manere putatur hodieque in Opido Briones
apud quos Bero fluvius, qui Vero Martiali, corrupte dicam, an consueta genti com-
mutatione Litterarum B & V? Suessitani, Livio; quorum appellationem adhuc superesse
volunt quidam in Sanguessa opido. Bergistani, qui apud eundem Livium lib.
xxxvi, Καρίσιοι denique, quorum apud Ptolemæum est mentio.
Regionis Caput hodie Pompelon; Πομπήλων apud Ptolemæum & Strabonem: nome-
n & nunc servans, Pampelona vulgo dicta. Vocemhanc per Ae diphthongon scri-
bendam innuit Lapis Tarraconensis, nisi Sculptoris manus aberrarit:

Quibusdam Pompeiopolis (quod à Cn. Pompeio Magno condita) & Martua dicitur:

page.notes: The map is an engraving with place names; its legends are not transcribed. Side notes in the right margin (Vascones, Berones, Suessitani, Bergistani, Metropolis Pompelon, Iturissa, Cascantum) are marked as notes. Some Greek and the final inscription line are damaged and uncertain; the last line of the page is partly illegible.
